analysis: Examined three files. (1) DaemonStateFile.swift adds optional diagnostic fields to the daemon state JSON: enabledModelsAtStart, enabledModelsAtLastSwitch and selectedModelRecovery. Existing fields already expose model IDs and selection lists. The new fields add only model IDs, timestamps and blocker strings. The file is written atomically with no access control change, and the write()/read() paths are unchanged. The new data does not carry prompts, keys, tokens, or authorization material, so it adds no new disclosure beyond model identity, which is already public via heartbeats (see T-041 residual metadata). The file is a diagnostic only. No authorization, attestation or trust decision is derived from it in the supplied code. (2) SelectedModelRecovery.swift is a new pure value-type scheduler with capped exponential backoff (30s to 600s), a 15s pause recheck and a 120s victim-idle minimum. It has no I/O, crypto or network surface. Availability is bounded by the backoff. The actual eviction and load logic lives in ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery, which is not supplied. Open integration question: whether the recovery path's eviction of unselected idle models can disturb in-flight requests, or interact with App Attest or add-on hold admission (TB-012/T-059, A-018), or with the prefix-cache lifecycle. This path is outside the supplied evidence, so no conclusion is drawn. (3) StartupPreloader.swift adds failedInsufficientMemory and notAttempted summary tracking, and makes isInsufficientMemoryLoad internal. It is bookkeeping only. The memory-admission and load behaviour is unchanged, and the string matching is not exposed publicly. No regression against the threat model identified. The unseen ProviderLoop consumers of these new fields remain a coverage limit.
